audit.why: 52.6% over 5513 games, and Darius owns every lane stage until Sylas is itemised. EVEN at 5.5/10 slightly undersells it but is defensible; the chart was the real problem.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[2] and win[4] said Skill and win[6] said Darius, while whys[2] and whys[4] describe Darius stages and whys[6] gives Sylas two-plus items. The packet chart reads Darius x6 then Sylas.
audit.why: Three rows contradicted their own explanations, and the last row was inverted against the entry's own late-game text.
audit.corrected: Levels 3 and 6 to Darius, 2+ items to Sylas at 4/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d both describe Abscond/Abduct as 'His dash + stun (recast pull)'. There is no stun. The recast pulls SYLAS to the enemy he hits, it does not hold you. The content layer also never names a Sylas ability (packet defect), and nothing states what Hijack actually does with your ultimate.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits.' A reader told to expect a stun will hold Flash for CC that never comes. On Hijack: Noxian Guillotine's damage 'is increased for each stack of Hemorrhage on the target', and Sylas has no way to apply Hemorrhage, so the stolen execute is base damage — the threat is the 460-range leap onto you, not the number.
audit.corrected: Stun claim removed, the recast described correctly, and Hijack's real effect stated with its 80/55/30s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere despite three of his four spells being on 6-13s.
audit.why: Abscond at 13s at rank 1 is the window the entry tells you to fight in, and it never says how long that window is.
audit.corrected: Abscond/Abduct 13s, Kingslayer 12s, Chain Lash 10s and Apprehend 26s at rank 1.

audit.why: tldr already rushes anti-heal, which is right — Kingslayer heals him off champions and is the reason his short trades reset.

edits.before: Sylas steals your R, but a full-stack Noxian Guillotine still executes him first; just don't feed him an easy ult-theft on a whiffed engage.
edits.after: Hijack takes your R, but he cannot stack Hemorrhage, so the stolen Guillotine is base damage — treat it as a 460-range leap onto you, not an execute.

edits.before: Sylas pokes with Q but has no answer to your pull threat at 1-2 — walk him down, sidestep the Q chain, and bleed him with Q Decimate.
edits.after: Sylas pokes with Chain Lash, which explodes again at the intersection — step off that point, then walk him down and bleed him with Q Decimate.

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. Darius E (Apprehend): Long early cooldown. Never throw this out predictably; save it explicitly to interrupt their dash trajectories mid-flight or catch their retreat paths. Darius Ghost: Your primary lethal enabler. Keep this tool ready to completely blow through ranged poke or instant slows across the lane.
edits.after: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — 13s at rank 1. The recast pulls him to you, so it is a gap-closer, not a hold. Bait it, then commit. - Kingslayer: 12s at rank 1 and it heals him off you — anti-heal before it. - Chain Lash: 10s, and it detonates a second time at the intersection point, so step off it. - Apprehend: 26s at rank 1, saved for the moment he lands, never thrown at the dash itself.

edits.before: His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: His dash, recast to chain himself to you. It is 13s at rank 1 — commit on that, never into it.

notes: Both cooldown fields called Abscond/Abduct a 'dash + stun'. It has no stun — the recast pulls Sylas to the target he hits. Corrected in both places. Hijack was dismissed with 'disregard his stolen ultimate'; the accurate version is that he cannot apply Hemorrhage, so your R in his hands is base true damage and the real threat is the leap, which is now stated. Chart contradicted its own whys and the packet in three rows, including an inverted 2+ items row.
